name: What should I do first if my kitchen floor is damaged and I want to replace it?

mainEntity.name: What should I do first if my kitchen floor is damaged and I want to replace it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start by identifying why the floor needs replacement and whether the cabinets, appliances, or nearby flooring will stay. A design-build assessment can check the visible floor, subfloor, transitions, moisture exposure, and the kitchen’s planned layout before materials are selected. Context: A torn, loose, stained, or repeatedly damaged surface may reflect an underlying moisture or leveling issue rather than a finish problem alone. Replacing flooring during a broader kitchen remodel may also affect cabinet and appliance sequencing. Key factors: - Water damage or leaks - Subfloor condition and flatness - Cabinet and appliance heights - Transitions to adjacent rooms Practical guidance: Photograph damaged areas, note soft spots or recurring leaks, and measure the kitchen and connected spaces before requesting a scope. Elite Remodeling & Design can coordinate flooring decisions with kitchen design and construction planning.
acceptedAnswer.description: First identify the damage source, check for moisture or soft spots, and decide whether cabinets, appliances, and nearby flooring will remain. A professional assessment should review the subfloor, transitions, and project sequence before you choose materials.
